details:
This is something I imagine unity can do, or do with a script. Vrchat needs a system, that goes "can all the meshes on this avatar be toggle on at the same time? Okay flowchart says no. that's a + to the rating, now rather than evaluating EVERYTHING ON THE AVATAR AT ONCE, what's the number of materials and polygons on the WORST case of what can be toggled on at one time? 
Because any smart person would make toggles turn each other OFF. 
For instance, on my avatar, there's shorts by default, i toggle on pants. I don't leave the shorts there. i toggle them off. There is no way the shorts AND pants can ever be on at the same time.  So why are we reading BOTH of those together as a worst case scenario? It's not like unity can't see the layers we've made to make these toggles. Is there really no way to see what CAN be on at one time, and then calculate THAT?
instead the system just goes "turn on all meshes, calculate how many polygons that is - very poor"
those meshes, if a smart person sets up the toggle, will never ever be rendered all at once like that.
or even, run through those toggles and get a high-low. like , jenny here's avatar has 5 different hair meshes, ranging from 3000 polygons and 1 material, to 20,000 polygons and 5 materials, so POTENTIALLY her avatar could be, and here's how this would show up over your head and in avatar stats 
{Poor - excellent} 
telling people that your avatar is in that range depending on what's turned on, and say jimmy's avatar is just high polygon everything. His would just get {very poor}
or {very poor - poor}
with how it is right now, it just turns on all meshes, and then grades you based on that
when a good setup means those meshes will never all be on at the same time
and thus not a performance hit
My avatar has 7 outfits, 30 or so meshes. but see, the pajamas DISABLE the other outfits, so you can't say "well you're rending all 208 thousand polygons at once" because no, it's not.
they're derendered
i have never caused anyone lag with my VERY POOR 208 thousand polygon avatar
So yes, my solution is some sort of system that instead -runs- the avatar, for instance the way unity does upon upload. 
Instead of turning on every mesh to check a total worst case, instead find what the avatar can -actually- be, depending on it's internal state machines. 
this way, avatars wouldn't always show up as VERY POOR and end up with players discriminating against others with a perfectly fine avatar that just has a lot of clothing items or accessories it can turn on, but are never ever all on at once. 
 (and can you not close my post while i'm editting it to be more verbose? thanks)
title: Better avatar stats system.
